prompt: Editorial on-model wedding photograph at night, vertical 9:16 frame. Photographed from behind her, the camera about 35 degrees to the right of straight behind and level with the ear, looking at the back of her right ear. Her face points directly away from the camera, so the whole face is hidden behind the back of her head and jaw. The back of the head, the nape and a low glossy dark bun wrapped in a white mogra gajra fill the left half of the frame; the right ear, seen from behind, sits in the right third. To the right of the ear there is only the side of the neck, the back edge of the jaw and loose hair, then the background. The cheek's outer edge never reaches the right side of the frame, and no eyelash, eye, eyebrow, temple or nose shows anywhere, not even as a silhouette against the lights. (Last time the head was only partly turned away, and an eyelash, the outer corner of an eye and the tail of an eyebrow showed past the cheek at the right edge of the frame; that must never happen.) One earring is worn tip-down on the earlobe of an Indian woman in her late thirties with warm wheatish skin, natural texture and fine downy hair at the nape; an oxblood raw-silk blouse at the shoulder. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly from the left stud, which faces the camera straight on, and ignore its background, plaster block and light. The piece: a stud, a 15 mm four-pointed star with concave sides, worn tip-down: 1 row of about 44 tiny round pave stones traces the outline; inside, 4 clear pear-cut stones, each in a polished frame with 1 bead prong at its point, aim out at the 4 tips; centre: 1 round clear stone in a bezel on a small 4-pointed plate; 8 slim open gaps flank the pears; 18k gold tone, high polish. Copy the left stud in reference 1 exactly. The pavé is only the single outer row along the 4 concave sides: there is no pavé between the pears and no second row around any pear. Each pear is one large faceted clear stone, not a cluster of small stones, in its own thin smooth polished frame. Its pointed end faces its tip of the star, its rounded end faces the centre, and one round bead prong sits at its point. Between each pear and the outline, and between neighbouring pears, 8 slim open windows show the skin through the piece. The centre is 1 round clear stone (round, not oval) in a smooth round bezel on a small flat 4-pointed plate in 18k gold tone, whose 4 points reach out between the pears. (Last time pavé dividers ran from the centre to the inner corners and filled the 8 windows, each pear became a glittery cluster of tiny stones, one pear was turned round, and the centre became an upright oval with no 4-pointed plate; all of that is wrong.) It must stay a sharp four-pointed star with an open pave outline around 4 outward-pointing pears, never a rounded four-leaf shape, never a solid pave face, never more than 4 pears. Do not redesign, restyle or resize it. SCALE, the most important instruction: the star is 15 mm tip to tip, the size of a shirt button. The ear, from the top of the helix to the bottom of the lobe, is about four star-heights tall. The star sits on the lobe, covers most of it and stops at the lobe's lower edge, never hanging below the lobe onto the jaw or neck. The ear is about a quarter of the frame height, so the star spans about one ninth of the frame width. There is a soft contact shadow on the lobe. (Last time the star was drawn about 24 mm, almost half the ear's height, and hung below the lobe onto the jaw; that is wrong.) WORLD: far behind, out of focus, the underside of a red and saffron striped wedding shamiana strung with hundreds of warm tungsten fairy lights, melting into large, soft, perfectly round bokeh discs. LIGHT: one large soft key from the left; one small hard specular kicker from above right draws a crisp edge along the gold tone and puts one pure-white catchlight in each pear and the centre stone. The gold tone stays the warm yellow of reference 1, never orange, copper or rose. The tungsten amber stays in the background bokeh, and the ear and the stud are lit by a neutral warm-white key. (Last time the tungsten turned the metal coppery orange.) COMPOSITION: the stud's centre sits 44 percent of the way down the frame and about 70 percent across. The top 35 percent is the dark crown of the head and calm, darker canopy bokeh, for a title. From 55 percent down, everything is calm nape, neck and blouse in soft shadow, for a caption band. (Last time the frame showed the whole back of the head and the stud sat 60 percent of the way down; come closer, so the ear is about a quarter of the frame height.) The photograph is clean, modern and pin-sharp: no VHS look, no scan lines, no star-shaped glints, no starburst on the fairy lights (they stay round soft discs), no lens flare, no glow; effects are added later. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no timestamps. No face, no eyes, no eyebrows. Only this one earring; no other jewellery. It must stay a sharp four-pointed star with an open pave outline around 4 outward-pointing pears, never a rounded four-leaf shape, never a solid pave face, never more than 4 pears.

prompt: Witty editorial still-life advertising photograph, vertical 9:16 frame, close and low at about 15 degrees: a plain black VHS video cassette from the 1990s lies flat on pooled oxblood raw silk, its matte black plastic face with one clear window showing brown tape wound on a white reel hub; a blank cream paper label strip runs along its front edge, completely blank. The camera is truly low, about 15 degrees above the top of the cassette, so the front edge with its blank label faces the lens almost square-on and looks tall, and the top face is a narrow, foreshortened band. On top of the cassette, near its front edge, the pair of earrings stands side by side a finger's width apart: the left one shows its barrel-shaped brushed front face, the right one is turned to show the C opening and the depth of the band. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. It confirms the brushed grain and the scale; leave out the cardamom pod. The piece: 1 pair of chunky hoops, each a short C of 1 wide, softly domed band: barrel-shaped front face 14 mm tall x 9.8 mm wide, band about 6 mm deep, rounded pillowy edges, smooth inner face, 0 stones, 0 visible hinge, post or ridge; soft brushed satin 18k gold tone with fine straight parallel brush lines, pale warm yellow. It must stay matte brushed satin, never mirror-polished, never silver tone, never ridged or hammered. Do not redesign, restyle or resize it. SCALE, the most important instruction: this is a full-size VHS cassette, 187 mm long, 103 mm deep and 25 mm thick, and each earring is only 14 mm tall and 9.8 mm wide, so the cassette is huge next to the pair. Each earring is clearly shorter than the cassette is thick. If an earring stood on the silk beside the cassette, its top would reach only a little above halfway up the cassette's front edge, the edge that carries the blank cream label strip. The camera is so close that only about 80 mm of the cassette's length fits across the frame: both ends of the cassette are outside the left and right edges of the frame, and the reel window is cut by the left edge. A dark, believable contact shadow sits under each piece where it stands on the plastic. (Last time this went wrong: the camera looked down from about 38 degrees, the left end of the cassette and most of its top fitted inside the frame, and each earring came out taller than the cassette is thick, almost twice its real size. That must not happen again: the earrings are small and the cassette is big.) LIGHT: one soft warm tungsten fill from the left; one small hard specular light right beside the lens, like a 1990s on-camera video light, throws a crisp hard drop shadow behind each piece and spreads into a soft wide sheen along the brushed dome, never a hot white spot. Each earring throws a crisp, hard-edged, dark drop shadow onto the black plastic behind it. The brushed metal shows one broad soft sheen and stays pale warm yellow all over: no pink, red or copper reflection bands from the silk on the metal, and no clipped white patch. (Last time the shadows were soft and fell away to the right, and a copper-pink stripe reflected from the silk crossed the lower part of the left earring.) Directly below the pair, the cassette's front edge with its wide blank cream label strip runs across the whole width of the frame, then the silk falls into soft shadow, calm for a caption band. (Last time the pair sat too low, with its bottoms 54 percent of the way down.) Palette: oxblood, cocoa, matte black, warm tungsten; the 18k gold tone is the only warm metal. The photograph is clean, modern and pin-sharp: no VHS look, no scan lines, no star-shaped glints, no lens flare, no glow; effects are added later. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no timestamps. No brand marks on the cassette; the label stays blank. The black plastic is plain: no embossed or moulded letters, numbers, dots, arrows or symbols on its rim, top or edges. The only texture is the fine square knurled grip pattern. (Last time a row of blurred embossed dots ran along the cassette's back rim.) No people, no face, no eyes, no eyebrows, no hands, no other jewellery, no water. It must stay matte brushed satin, never mirror-polished, never silver tone, never ridged or hammered.

prompt: Editorial on-model wedding photograph, vertical 9:16 frame, full bleed, the photograph filling the frame edge to edge with no plain bands or borders (one earlier take was padded with flat plum bands top and bottom). A wide woven zari border of warm metallic thread crosses the lower part of the frame on a diagonal, softly out of focus, and at the very top the skirt falls away into soft, round, warm tungsten fairy-light bokeh. She wears the ring on the middle finger between the knuckle and the first finger joint, the butterfly seen face-on and flat to the camera exactly as in reference 1, the wingspan across the finger and the body bar along it. The butterfly stands upright in the frame, its body bar vertical and its two larger upper wings toward the top of the frame, never turned or tilted (one earlier take turned it about 45 degrees off upright). Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. Use reference 2 only for how the piece sits on the body and its true size there; take nothing else from it: not the person, her face, lips, clothes or background. On top, 1 solid 4-wing butterfly, 18 mm wide, each wing in a raised polished rim, filled with dense pale lavender-lilac micro pave, 1 plain polished body bar, 0 antennae. The micro pave is about 150 separate round lilac stones, about 4 or 5 across a 3 mm patch, with tiny 18k gold tone grain beads between them, exactly the stone size of reference 1, never a fine glitter crust (one earlier take made grains a third that size). The body bar is a slim straight rod with rounded ends, as in reference 1, never a pointed lozenge or seed shape. Because the rail is slim, the 4 windows stay wide open as in reference 1: a tall open gap inside each upper flag, an open triangle inside each pointed lower lobe, with skin or silk showing through.
